title: Sell Mineral Rights in Kalkaska, MI
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Kalkaska, MI
metaDescription: Kalkaska County seat mineral rights owner? Real Antrim Shale core history around the village. Get an honest evaluation of what your interest is worth.
heroLead: Kalkaska is the county seat, and it's also dead center of some of the heaviest Antrim Shale well density anywhere in the trend, which means the odds your family's land got drilled during the boom are genuinely good.
intro: The village of Kalkaska sits in Kalkaska County, part of the historic core of the Antrim Shale trend, and the sections around town saw dense drilling during the Section 29 tax-credit boom of the late 1980s and 1990s. If your family owned land in or near Kalkaska during that period, there's a strong chance a well was drilled nearby and a lease is still technically active today, held by production decades later.

sections.heading: Heavy well density around the village
paragraphs: Kalkaska sits in one of the more heavily drilled parts of the Antrim core, which is good for owners in one specific way, there's likely real, documented production history behind your interest rather than an unclear leased-but-never-drilled situation. It's not necessarily good news on value, since these wells are now decades old and well into their mature decline.
We check current production for your specific section before quoting anything, since even in a dense area like this, individual well performance varies.

sections.heading: Register of deeds and title records in Kalkaska
paragraphs: As the county seat, Kalkaska is home to the Kalkaska County register of deeds, where the recorded chain of title, deeds, probate records, and leases, for mineral interests across the county is kept. If you're not sure exactly what you own or which well your interest ties to, that office is the starting point, along with any division order you may have from an operator.

sections.heading: What we need to evaluate a Kalkaska interest
paragraphs: Send your deed or probate document, any royalty statements or division orders you've received, and the legal description if you have it. Because well density here is high, we're often able to identify your specific well quickly once we have the section, township, and range.
If multiple family members share the interest, note how it's currently divided if you know. We'll check current production before saying anything about value.

faqs.question: Is Kalkaska village in the core of the Antrim Shale trend?
faqs.answer: Yes, Kalkaska County is one of the historic core counties, and the sections immediately around the village saw fairly dense drilling during the 1980s and 1990s boom.

faqs.question: Why is my Kalkaska-area royalty check smaller than it used to be?
faqs.answer: Wells here are decades into a long, flat decline typical of mature Antrim Shale production, so volumes and checks are a fraction of what they were during the well's early years.

faqs.question: Where do I find the recorded chain of title for mineral rights in Kalkaska?
faqs.answer: The Kalkaska County register of deeds, located in the village, holds recorded deeds, probate records, and leases for the entire county.

faqs.question: Should I expect a lump-sum offer or ongoing royalty income for a Kalkaska interest?
faqs.answer: It depends on your situation. We'll lay out both the lump-sum number and what continuing to hold might look like, and let you decide which fits your circumstances better.
